text: MistTrack: Bitget Exploiter Attempted to Route Stolen Funds via Chainflip but Broker Rejected According to on-chain monitoring by SlowMist's tracking arm MistTrack, the Bitget exploiter attempted to move stolen funds through the cross-chain liquidity protocol Chainflip, but the transaction was rejected at the broker interface ("deposit rejected by the broker"). The protocol did not freeze the capital but instead refunded the deposit directly back to the sender, effectively preventing the attacker from routing the exploit proceeds through the network. SlowMist founder Cos stated that cross-chain liquidity protocol Chainflip is indeed making significant efforts to block North Korean hacking groups from laundering stolen funds, but unfortunately, AML and KYT solutions are lagging behind the speed of the attackers' laundering operations. The laundering syndicates employ automated tools to split substantial funds into smaller amounts and bridge them across multiple blockchains; if intercepted, flagged by risk controls, or refunded, they immediately pivot to the next laundering route. Ultimately, these proceeds are converted into Bitcoin and further obfuscated via CoinJoin. — link
